content: 1. Tecovirimat is a weak inducer of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It can reduce the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should also be monitored for effectiveness if used concurrently with tecovirimat. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. After discontinuing cobicistat, a one-week washout period should be allowed before increasing the temsirolimus dose to its original level. 3. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of teniposide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide (AF) by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dosage of the P-gp substrate as recommended in its product labeling and monitor closely. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of theophylline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of thioridazine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be necessary when co-administered. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of ticagrelor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of timolol by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels of tisotumab vedotin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to unconjugated MMAE, raising the risk of adverse effects. 16. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of tofacitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily. 17. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid concomitant use of P-gp inhibitors. The interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 20. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of toremifene by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., less than 14 days), administer the inhibitor one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tramadol by affecting both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. A reduced dose of tramadol may be required. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trazodone by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Trazodone is a substrate of both enzymes, and cobicistat inhibits their activity. 24. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of triazolam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Triazolam and oral midazolam are extensively metabolized by CYP3A, and their co-administration with cobicistat may cause large increases in benzodiazepine concentrations, potentially leading to serious or life-threatening events such as prolonged sedation or respiratory depression. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose and monitoring for response. 26. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Tucatinib significantly increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid using tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 31. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vadadustat may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, necessitating dose adjustments based on product labeling. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by affecting both CYP2E1 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Reduce the vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day if weight is over 50 kg. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 37. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated with venetoclax during the initial ramp-up dosing phase. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used after the ramp-up phase, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 75%. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of venlafaxine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of verapamil by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 41. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with increased systemic exposure to vinblastine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant side effects. If withholding the regimen for a prolonged period, consider initiating a revised regimen without a CYP3A or P-gp inhibitor. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vincristine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with increased systemic exposure to vincristine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant side effects. If withholding the regimen for a prolonged period, consider initiating a revised regimen without a CYP3A or P-gp inhibitor. 44. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity when co-administered with voclosporin. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 47. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 48. Voriconazole increases the levels of elvitegravir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat also increases the levels of voriconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended unless the benefit/risk assessment justifies its use. 49. Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of warfarin by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of warfarin through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor INR more frequently if co-administered with inhibitors of these isoenzymes and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 50. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous zanubrutinib dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 51. Zinc decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Administer elvitegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after polyvalent cation-containing products. 52. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
